blockers.appliesTo: CLAUDE-V38-B1 route (2) / PTCB-V38-B2 — the capability proof was replaced by a check a kexec-capable kernel generally passes
blockers.title: kexecSymbolAbsence proves kexec-absent from the non-occurrence of symbol-name strings in the decompressed payload, but a Linux kernel image does not normally store those names as contiguous plain bytes, so the check passes for kexec-capable kernels and its only backstop is explicitly optional
blockers.whatTheClauseSays: kexecSymbolAbsence carries standing 'STRUCTURAL PROOF', a haystack of 'decompressed payload P only', a list of eleven forbidden strings including __x64_sys_kexec_load, __arm64_sys_kexec_file_load, kernel_kexec, machine_kexec and crash_kexec, and the rule 'None of the forbiddenUtf8 strings MAY occur as a contiguous UTF-8 byte sequence in P. Any hit refuses. This is the structural kexec-absent proof.' result.kexecCapability is then 'exactly kexec-absent iff kexecSymbolAbsence succeeds', and signedAttestation adds 'Signed carriage MUST NOT replace kexecSymbolAbsence.' So the entire capability claim rests on this search.
blockers.theDefect: The check assumes the payload contains those function names as contiguous plain byte sequences. A Linux kernel image does not generally satisfy that assumption. When the kernel's symbol table is built in, names are held in a token-compressed table and expanded at run time rather than stored as whole contiguous strings; when it is not built in, no symbol names are present at all. In neither case does a search for a contiguous occurrence of __x64_sys_kexec_load find anything, whether or not the kexec entry points are compiled in. Function names appear as plain contiguous strings only when some build option that emits them happens to be enabled. This contract requires no such option and never mentions the question: I searched the whole artifact for kallsyms, BTF, symtab and CONFIG_KALLSYMS and each occurs zero times. The proof's detection power therefore depends on an unstated, unrequired property of the build, and when that property does not hold the search returns no hit and the derivation returns kexec-absent.
blockers.whyTheBackstopDoesNotHold: IKCONFIG would catch the case, and this generation deliberately removes it from that role. ikconfig.standing is 'CORROBORATION only. MUST NOT be the structural proof', and ifPresent closes with the sentence that decides this: 'Absence of IKCONFIG does not refuse if kexecSymbolAbsence succeeds.' So a kernel built without the embedded configuration has no second check at all. I credit that when IKCONFIG is present the conflicting-y-or-m rule still refuses, which is a real retained safeguard for that subset of images; but the contract's declared structural proof is the weaker check, and the combination of kexec compiled in and IKCONFIG absent is expressly permitted to pass.
blockers.theFailureDirection: This is the property that makes it a blocker rather than an over-refusal. The v38 mechanism I rejected could at least be made to fail by an image whose embedded configuration disagreed with its code; it correlated with the truth in the honest case and failed only under a crafted or careless build. This mechanism returns the passing answer for the ordinary case, so an entirely honest kexec-enabled distro kernel with no embedded configuration is certified kexec-absent. Since the no-replacement closure rests on that certification, the profile then attests that the executing kernel is the launched one for a machine on which replacement remains possible.
blockers.howToConfirmItCheaply: The reserved G22 vectors are the right place: take any stock kexec-enabled kernel image for either in-scope architecture, run the eleven-string search over its decompressed payload, and observe whether a hit occurs. If no hit occurs, the check has certified a kexec-capable kernel. That vector is not among the reserved set and should be added whichever repair route is taken.
blockers.requiredRepair: Make the capability proof one that a kexec-capable kernel actually fails, and say what it assumes about the image. Three routes, any of which suffices. (1) Pin the encoding: require the payload to carry its symbol names in a named, version-pinned form, specify the decoding operation for that form, run the forbidden-symbol test against decoded names rather than raw bytes, and refuse when the image does not carry names in the pinned form so the test cannot pass vacuously. (2) Return the configuration check to structural standing: require IKCONFIG rather than making it optional, keep the completeness and explicit-disabled-form rules v38 established, and supply the authenticated builder binding Codex asked for at PTCB-V38-B2 so the configuration is tied to the build rather than merely extracted from the image. (3) Compare against a signed reference: measure the decompressed payload and require its digest to equal a signed reference for a build the signer attests is kexec-absent, which also answers the entry-to-payload question Codex raised at PTCB-V38-B1. Under any route, state the assumption the check makes about how the image represents the property, and add the stock-kernel vector above.

repairsVerified.finding: PTCB-V38-S1 — the arm64 and inner-gzip parsers remained underdetermined
repairsVerified.result: REPAIRED, on every element Codex enumerated. The zimg scan is confined to loaded PE sections and 4-byte aligned, with exactly one match taking the zboot branch, zero taking the uncompressed branch and more than one refusing, which closes the incidental-zimg case. The zboot header must lie wholly within the same loaded section and its payload range must satisfy peJoin.loadedRange, with compressed_type required to equal the magic detection and disagreement refusing. The magic-free fallback is gone: the uncompressed branch now requires exactly one loaded executable section with 41 52 4d 64 at section-relative 0x38 and states 'No magic-free fallback.' The gzip rules Codex asked for are present as a closed set: C is capped at 8 MiB, 'Concatenated extra gzip members after the first refuse', and 'Trailing non-gzip bytes after that member refuse', alongside the existing 128 MiB payload ceiling.

repairsVerified.finding: PTCB-V38-B1 — the PE-entry-to-payload relation was an untestable assertion
repairsVerified.result: PARTIALLY REPAIRED. peJoin.notInert is rewritten as an operation rather than a requirement: 'the selected payload is the unique range named by the official x86 header at the pinned offsets, or by the unique loaded-section zimg / 0x38 Image header. That closes the decoy-header search Codex named and is checkable against the header and section table. It does not establish that the code at the entry point consumes that payload, which is what the finding's first sentence asked for; Codex's three suggested routes were a canonical stub identity with an exact entry relation, a signed builder predicate covering that relation, or a measurement of the decompressed executed payload, and none is supplied. limitsOfThisReview: I reviewed both predecessor verdicts' findings, the replacement capability proof, the architecture and decompression rules, the closed change roster, the pin chain, the live register/COORD/file-04 carries and the authority refusals. Paths outside this round's roster were checked only for unchangedness, which is how the escaping path surfaced. CLAUDE-V39-B1 rests on how Linux kernel images represent symbol names and on the artifact's own silence about that representation; I have stated the confirmation vector explicitly so the finding can be settled empirically against a stock kernel rather than argued, and the repair routes I name do not require agreeing with my reading, since each makes the check's assumption explicit and refuses when it does not hold. The reserved G22 vectors remain unpopulated and were not evaluated.
summary: REJECT at 1 blocker and 1 SHOULD-FIX. Custody is clean: subject unmoved at 8e081339... and 0444 at both ends, 59/59 chain pins reproduce, both frozen v38 verdicts reproduce with no replacement, reviewGuidance a pure append, the sole DR-126 row quoted byte-exactly, all remeasurement pins reproducing, and all 36 D-096 occurrences refusals. Most of this generation is good work. Codex's arm64 and gzip finding is repaired on every element — aligned loaded-section scanning, zero-one-many resolution, the magic-free fallback removed, compressor agreement required, concatenated members and trailing bytes refused, and both size ceilings present. The projection finding is repaired, the dropped kexec_loaded condition is restored, the decoy-header search is closed by a header-uniqueness operation, and buildProvenance is withdrawn from the proof path with my v38 reasoning written into notThis. The problem is what now carries the capability claim. kexecSymbolAbsence is declared the structural proof, and result.kexecCapability is kexec-absent if and only if it succeeds, but it succeeds by finding no contiguous occurrence of eleven function-name strings in the decompressed payload. A Linux kernel image does not normally hold those names that way: with the in-kernel symbol table built in they are token-compressed and expanded at run time, and without it they are absent entirely, so an ordinary kexec-enabled kernel yields no hit. The contract never states this assumption — kallsyms, BTF, symtab and CONFIG_KALLSYMS each occur zero times in the artifact — and it removes the check that would have caught the case, since IKCONFIG is now corroboration only and 'Absence of IKCONFIG does not refuse if kexecSymbolAbsence succeeds.' The result is a proof whose failure direction is open: an honest kexec-enabled kernel with no embedded configuration is certified kexec-absent, and the no-replacement closure built on that certification then attests the launched kernel as the running one on a machine where replacement is still possible. Any of three repairs closes it — pin and decode the name representation, restore the configuration check to structural standing with the builder binding Codex asked for, or compare a measurement of the decompressed payload against a signed kexec-absent reference, which would also finish PTCB-V38-B1. The second finding is smaller: authenticatedKernelMember was correctly rewritten for the projection repair but sits outside every roster root, so basedOn.method's assertion that unnamed paths are unchanged is false, exactly as at v34.
